correctness.rationale: For hub-free subsets, each occupied blade needs at least \(\lfloor m_i/2floor+1\) selected vertices, and minimality forces exactly one threshold-sized blade. For hub-containing subsets, no blade may exceed \(\lfloor m_i/2floor\), otherwise a proper hub-free alliance is included. Hub feasibility requires \(x\ge\lfloor M/2floor\), while the peripheral restrictions imply \(x\le\sum_i\lfloor m_i/2floor=\lfloor M/2floor-\lfloor o/2floor\). Thus exactly \(o\le1\) permits hub cases and all blades must have their half-order selections. The converse minimality checks every proper subset, via hub omission or strict decrease in \(x\). The two disjoint cases yield the enumerator, upper cardinalities, parity transition and gaps. The standalone adjacency-based verifier exhaustively compared 537,880 subsets in 136 profiles; these finite checks support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The exact distribution of all globally minimal alliances answers the enumerative counterpart to an actively studied graph-parameter problem, for nonuniform clique-blade orders. More than a scalar optimum, the theorem isolates a structural obstacle determined by the number of odd blades, and establishes a sharp parity-driven decrease of the upper parameter as vertices are added. Even uniform blades realize arbitrarily long intervals of unattainable globally minimal alliance sizes. Such extreme discontinuity and complete solution-family classification are natural targets for further study of alliance minimality and induced clique-block graph structure, without asserting an unproved downstream general theorem.
